The right opportunity will support your professional growth while respecting your personal life—because sustainable success requires both.## Technology Infrastructure and ","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1},{"type":"link","fields":{"url":"/resume-formatting-9-essential-best-practices-for-ats-success","newTab":false,"linkType":"custom"},"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"ATS","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":null},{"mode":"normal","text":" Compatibility","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"When evaluating a job offer, most candidates focus on salary and benefits while overlooking a critical factor: the company's technology infrastructure. The tools, systems, and digital platforms an organization uses directly impact your daily workflow, professional development, and long-term career trajectory.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"As someone who has spent years analyzing how Applicant Tracking Systems filter candidates, I've learned that a company's approach to technology reveals much about its operational maturity and commitment to employee success. Understanding the employer's tech stack during your job offer assessment helps you gauge whether you'll have the resources needed to perform effectively and grow professionally.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Evaluating Digital Tools and Platforms","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Start by asking specific questions about the technology you'll use daily. What project management tools does the team rely on? Which communication platforms are standard? What software will you need to master to succeed in the role?","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Companies investing in modern, industry-standard tools typically demonstrate a commitment to efficiency and employee productivity. Conversely, organizations relying heavily on outdated systems may signal budget constraints, resistance to change, or limited technical leadership.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Consider how the technology aligns with your existing skills and career goals. If you're building expertise in specific platforms or methodologies, ensure the new role provides opportunities to deepen that knowledge rather than requiring you to work with legacy systems that may limit your marketability.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Understanding ATS and Recruitment Technology","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"The sophistication of a company's Applicant Tracking System offers insights into their hiring maturity and organizational processes. Companies using advanced ATS platforms often have more structured onboarding, better documentation, and clearer career progression frameworks.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"During your conversations, inquire about how the company manages talent acquisition and internal mobility. Do they use their ATS for performance tracking and succession planning? Can employees apply for internal positions through a transparent system? These details reveal whether the organization has invested in infrastructure that supports career development.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"For tech roles specifically, understanding ATS compatibility becomes even more important. Companies that optimize their hiring technology typically maintain similar standards across their operational systems, creating environments where technical professionals can thrive.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Assessing Technology Training and Support","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Beyond the tools themselves, evaluate the support structure surrounding technology adoption. Does the company provide comprehensive training for new platforms? Is there dedicated IT support when technical issues arise? Are employees encouraged to pursue certifications or professional development in relevant technologies?","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Organizations with robust technology training programs demonstrate they value continuous learning and understand that tools are only effective when people know how to use them properly. This commitment often extends beyond technology to broader professional development initiatives.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Ask about the onboarding process for technical systems. A well-structured technology onboarding program suggests the company has thoughtfully designed employee experiences and invested in retention strategies.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Technology Infrastructure as a Career Catalyst","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"The right technology infrastructure can accelerate your career by exposing you to industry-standard tools, automating routine tasks, and enabling you to focus on high-value work. Conversely, inadequate technology can create frustration, limit your productivity, and slow your professional growth.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Consider whether the company's technology choices align with industry trends and future demands. Working with cutting-edge platforms positions you for advancement, while experience with obsolete systems may make future job searches more challenging.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"For those in technical fields, the employer's tech stack becomes part of your professional portfolio. Each tool you master, each system you optimize, and each platform you implement adds to your marketability and expertise.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Questions to Ask During Job Offer Assessment","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Before accepting an offer, gather specific information about technology infrastructure:","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"ul","type":"list","start":1,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"type":"listitem","value":1,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"What core platforms and tools does the team use daily?","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"listitem","value":2,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"How often does the company update or upgrade its technology systems?","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"listitem","value":3,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"What is the process for requesting new tools or software?","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"listitem","value":4,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Does the company provide technology stipends or equipment allowances?","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"listitem","value":5,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"How does the organization handle cybersecurity and data protection?","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"listitem","value":6,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"What collaboration tools support remote or hybrid work arrangements?","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"}],"listType":"bullet","direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"These questions demonstrate your strategic thinking while providing concrete information for your decision-making process. The quality and transparency of the responses often reveal as much as the answers themselves.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Technology infrastructure assessment isn't about finding the company with the flashiest tools. It's about ensuring the organization provides the digital foundation you need to perform effectively, develop professionally, and advance your career goals. This evaluation becomes an essential component of comprehensive job offer assessment in 2026's technology-driven workplace.## Creating Your Job Offer Assessment Framework","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"id":"699a520df07ac487cb001b16","type":"upload","value":{"id":262,"site":1,"alt":"Job Offer Assessment Framework","prefix":"media","updatedAt":"2026-02-21T15:54:56.155Z","createdAt":"2026-02-21T15:54:56.155Z","url":"/api/media/file/job%20offer%20assessment%209%20simple%20steps%20for%20smart%20decisions-sec_8-75147a7e0d9.png","thumbnailURL":null,"filename":"job offer assessment 9 simple steps for smart decisions-sec_8-75147a7e0d9.png","mimeType":"image/png","filesize":1341659,"width":1024,"height":1024,"focalX":50,"focalY":50},"fields":{},"format":"","version":3,"relationTo":"media"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"A structured job offer assessment framework transforms overwhelming decisions into clear, objective evaluations. Rather than relying on gut feelings alone, creating a systematic approach helps you weigh competing factors and make choices aligned with your career trajectory.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"The most effective frameworks combine quantitative scoring with qualitative reflection. This dual approach ensures you consider both measurable elements like compensation and intangible factors like cultural fit.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"The Weighted Criteria Method","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Start by identifying your top evaluation categories. Common areas include compensation, career growth, work-life balance, company culture, location, and benefits. Assign each category a weight based on personal importance, ensuring all weights total 100%.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"For example, if career growth matters most to you, assign it 30%. If work-life balance is equally critical, give it 30%. Distribute remaining percentages across other factors like compensation (20%), culture (15%), and benefits (5%).","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Next, score each job offer on a scale of 1-10 for every category. Multiply each score by its weight, then sum the results. This produces a weighted total score that reflects your priorities rather than treating all factors equally.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Building Your Decision Matrix","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Create a simple comparison table with job offers as columns and evaluation criteria as rows. This visual layout makes it easy to spot strengths and weaknesses across opportunities.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Include both objective data (salary figures, vacation days, commute time) and subjective assessments (team dynamics, manager compatibility, mission alignment). Color-code cells to highlight areas where offers excel or fall short.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Consider adding a \"deal-breaker\" row to identify non-negotiable requirements. If an offer fails to meet these baseline standards, no amount of scoring in other areas can compensate.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Incorporating Long-Term Career Goals","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Your framework should extend beyond immediate satisfaction to evaluate strategic career positioning. Ask how each offer advances your three-year and five-year professional objectives.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Assess skill development opportunities, industry positioning, and network expansion potential. An offer with slightly lower compensation but significantly better learning opportunities may score higher when weighted for long-term growth.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Document your reasoning for each score. This written record helps you articulate your decision to others and provides a reference point if you face similar choices in the future.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Testing Your Framework","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Before finalizing decisions, run sensitivity analyses. Adjust category weights to see how scores shift. If small weight changes dramatically alter rankings, you may need to refine your priorities or gather more information.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Share your framework with trusted mentors or advisors. Their external perspective can reveal blind spots or help you recalibrate weights that don't truly reflect your values.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Remember that frameworks support decision-making but don't replace judgment. If your systematic evaluation conflicts with strong intuition, explore that disconnect before proceeding. The best decisions integrate both analytical rigor and self-awareness.## Red Flags and Warning Signs to Watch For","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Even the most attractive job offer can hide serious problems beneath the surface. Learning to recognize warning signs during the evaluation process protects you from costly career mistakes and ensures you make decisions aligned with your long-term goals.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"High Turnover and Revolving Door Patterns","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Frequent staff changes signal deeper organizational issues. When you notice multiple people have held the same position in a short timeframe, or when your interview panel includes several new hires, investigate further. Ask directly about turnover rates and average tenure in the role.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Pay attention to how the hiring manager responds to these questions. Defensive reactions or vague explanations often indicate cultural problems or unrealistic expectations that drive employees away.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Vague or Evasive Answers During Interviews","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Clarity matters when evaluating any opportunity. If interviewers cannot articulate clear job responsibilities, performance metrics, or reporting structures, the organization likely lacks direction. This ambiguity creates frustration and sets you up for misaligned expectations.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Watch for evasiveness around compensation details, benefits enrollment timelines, or company financial health. Legitimate employers provide transparent information about these fundamental aspects of employment.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Pressure Tactics and Artificial Urgency","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Employers who rush your decision-making process often have something to hide. Phrases like \"we need an answer by tomorrow\" or \"other candidates are waiting\" create artificial pressure designed to prevent thorough evaluation.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Respectable organizations understand that accepting a job offer represents a significant life decision. They allow reasonable time for consideration and welcome thoughtful questions throughout the process.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Unrealistic Expectations and Role Inflation","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Be cautious when job descriptions require expertise across too many unrelated areas or promise rapid advancement without clear pathways. These inflated expectations often lead to burnout and disappointment.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Compare the stated responsibilities with the offered compensation and support resources. Significant mismatches suggest the employer undervalues the role or lacks understanding of what success requires.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Poor Communication and Disorganization","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"The hiring process reveals how an organization operates daily. Missed interview appointments, delayed responses, or contradictory information from different team members indicate systemic communication problems.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"If basic coordination fails during recruitment—when companies typically showcase their best—expect worse once you join. Professional organizations maintain consistent, respectful communication throughout the hiring journey.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Trust Your Professional Instincts","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Your intuition draws from accumulated experience and pattern recognition. When something feels off, even if you cannot immediately identify the specific issue, take that signal seriously. Step back and analyze what triggered your concern.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Combine instinct with objective evaluation. Document specific observations that caused discomfort, then research whether these patterns align with known warning signs. This balanced approach prevents both overlooking genuine problems and rejecting opportunities based solely on nervousness.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Recognizing red flags requires practice and self-awareness. The investment in careful observation during job offer assessment protects your career trajectory and ensures your next move advances your professional goals rather than creating new obstacles.## Negotiation Strategies and Building Leverage","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Negotiation is an interpersonal decision-making process that becomes necessary when parties cannot achieve their objectives independently. Understanding this fundamental principle transforms how you approach job offer discussions—it's not adversarial, but collaborative problem-solving.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Successful negotiation requires preparation, strategic timing, and clear communication. The process involves understanding both your needs and the employer's constraints, then finding creative solutions that benefit everyone involved.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Timing Your Negotiation","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Never negotiate until you have a written offer in hand. Verbal promises lack enforceability and can disappear during formalization. Once you receive the official offer, take time to review it thoroughly before responding.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Request 24 to 48 hours to consider the offer, even if you're excited. This pause demonstrates thoughtfulness and gives you space to prepare your counteroffer strategy. Employers expect candidates to take time for such important decisions.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Avoid negotiating too early in the interview process. Discussing compensation before the employer has decided they want you significantly weakens your position. Wait until they've invested time and resources in selecting you as their top candidate.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Building Your Negotiation Leverage","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Leverage comes from having alternatives and demonstrating unique value. If you're interviewing with multiple companies, each offer strengthens your position with others. You don't need to disclose specific numbers, but indicating you're considering other opportunities creates urgency.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Document your accomplishments and how they relate to the role. Specific examples of past results—revenue generated, processes improved, teams led—justify higher compensation. Frame these contributions in terms of value you'll bring to the new organization.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Research market rates thoroughly using salary surveys, industry reports, and professional networks. Knowledge of comparable positions at similar companies provides objective data to support your requests. Geographic location, company size, and industry sector all influence appropriate compensation ranges.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"What's Negotiable Beyond Salary","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Base salary represents just one component of your total compensation package. Many elements offer negotiation flexibility, sometimes more readily than cash compensation.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Consider negotiating:","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"ul","type":"list","start":1,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"type":"listitem","value":1,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Sign-on bonuses","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":1,"version":1},{"mode":"normal","text":": One-time payments that don't affect ongoing salary budgets","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textFormat":1},{"type":"listitem","value":2,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Performance bonuses","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":1,"version":1},{"mode":"normal","text":": Target percentages and achievement metrics","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textFormat":1},{"type":"listitem","value":3,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Equity compensation","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":1,"version":1},{"mode":"normal","text":": Stock options, RSUs, or profit-sharing arrangements","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textFormat":1},{"type":"listitem","value":4,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Vacation costs","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textFormat":1},{"type":"listitem","value":7,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Relocation assistance","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":1,"version":1},{"mode":"normal","text":": Moving expenses, temporary housing, travel costs","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textFormat":1},{"type":"listitem","value":8,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Title structure","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textFormat":1},{"type":"listitem","value":9,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Start consideration","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textFormat":1}],"listType":"bullet","direction":"ltr","textFormat":1},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Companies often have more flexibility with non-salary items, especially when salary ranges are constrained by internal equity or budget limitations.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Effective Counteroffer Techniques","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Frame your counteroffer positively, expressing enthusiasm for the opportunity while presenting your request. Begin by thanking them for the offer and reiterating your interest in the position and company.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Use specific numbers rather than ranges. Requesting a salary between two amounts signals you'll accept the lower figure. State your desired compensation clearly, supported by research and your qualifications.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Present multiple items simultaneously rather than negotiating serially. If you ask for salary adjustment first, receive it, then request additional vacation, you appear perpetually unsatisfied. Instead, present a complete package: \"I'm excited about this opportunity. Based on my research and experience, I was expecting compensation in the range of $X, along with Y vacation days and Z professional development budget.\"","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Avoid ultimatums unless you're genuinely prepared to walk away. Statements like \"I need $X or I can't accept\" create win-lose dynamics that damage relationships. Instead, frame requests as questions: \"Is there flexibility in the salary range?\" or \"What would it take to reach $X?\"","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"The Four-Step Negotiation Process","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"According to negotiation frameworks, successful negotiations follow a structured process. First, prepare thoroughly by understanding your priorities, researching market standards, and identifying your walk-away point.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Second, exchange information openly. Share your perspective on fair compensation while listening to the employer's constraints and priorities. This dialogue often reveals creative solutions neither party initially considered.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Third, bargain collaboratively. Present your counteroffer with supporting rationale, then work together to find mutually acceptable terms. Be prepared to make strategic concessions on lower-priority items to gain ground on what matters most.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Fourth, close and commit. Once you reach agreement, confirm all terms in writing before accepting. Ensure the revised offer letter reflects everything discussed, including verbal promises about future reviews, bonuses, or other commitments.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Maintaining Positive Relationships","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Negotiation sets the tone for your future working relationship. Approach discussions professionally, focusing on mutual benefit rather than winning. Remember that the person negotiating with you—often your future manager or HR partner—will be your colleague.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Stay respectful and appreciative throughout the process. Acknowledge when the employer makes concessions and express gratitude for their flexibility. Even if you don't receive everything requested, recognize their efforts to accommodate your needs.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Be honest about your constraints and priorities. If work-life balance matters more than maximum salary, say so. Transparency builds trust and helps employers craft offers that genuinely meet your needs within their constraints.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Never make threats or comparisons that belittle the organization. Saying \"Company X offered me more\" creates resentment, while \"Based on market research for this role and geography, I was expecting a range of $X-Y\" presents objective information.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"When to Walk Away","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Sometimes negotiation reveals fundamental misalignment between your needs and what the employer can offer. If the gap is too large—whether in compensation, role responsibilities, or other critical factors—walking away demonstrates self-respect and career wisdom.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Decline offers professionally, thanking them for their time and consideration. Maintain positive relationships, as industries are smaller than they appear. Today's declined offer might lead to a better opportunity with the same organization in the future.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Trust your instincts during negotiation. If the employer responds to reasonable requests with pressure tactics, defensiveness, or unwillingness to discuss terms, these behaviors signal potential cultural issues. How they treat you during negotiation previews how they'll treat you as an employee.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Preparing for Common Objections","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Employers may respond to counteroffers with standard objections. Prepare responses in advance so you can address concerns confidently.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"If they cite budget constraints, explore non-salary alternatives or ask about timeline for future increases. \"I understand the current budget limitations. Could we revisit compensation at my six-month review based on performance?\"","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"If they mention internal equity, acknowledge the concern while emphasizing your unique qualifications. \"I appreciate the need for internal fairness. My experience in [specific area] brings immediate value in [specific way], which I believe justifies the adjustment.\"","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"If they claim the offer is final, test gently: \"I understand this represents your standard offer. Given my background in [area], is there any flexibility in [specific component]?\" Often \"final\" offers have room for adjustment when candidates present compelling rationale.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Negotiation is a normal, expected part of the hiring process. Employers anticipate counteroffers and respect candidates who advocate professionally for themselves. The skills you demonstrate during negotiation—preparation, communication, problem-solving—showcase the same capabilities that will make you valuable in the role.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Sources","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"tag":"ul","type":"list","start":1,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"type":"listitem","value":1,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"type":"link","fields":{"url":"https://www.pon.harvard.edu/daily/negotiation-skills-daily/what-is-negotiation/","newTab":false,"linkType":"custom"},"format":"","indent":0,"version":3,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"What is Negotiation? - Program on Negotiation at Harvard Law School","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"listitem","value":2,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"type":"link","fields":{"url":"https://online.hbs.edu/blog/post/steps-of-negotiation","newTab":false,"linkType":"custom"},"format":"","indent":0,"version":3,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"4 Steps of the Negotiation Process - Harvard Business School Online","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"listitem","value":3,"format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"type":"link","fields":{"url":"https://online.stanford.edu/how-improve-your-negotiation-skills-practical-guide-workplace","newTab":false,"linkType":"custom"},"format":"","indent":0,"version":3,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"How to Improve Your Negotiation Skills - Stanford Online","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"linebreak","version":1}],"direction":"ltr"}],"listType":"bullet","direction":"ltr"},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Making Strategic Career Decisions That Align With Your Goals","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":null},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[],"direction":null,"textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Ultimately, accepting a job offer should be a strategic move that aligns with where you want to go, not just a reaction to where you are. This perspective has shaped my approach to career coaching and empowered countless professionals to make informed and fulfilling career choices.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[],"direction":null,"textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Throughout this guide, you've explored the nine essential steps of job offer assessment—from analyzing compensation packages and company culture to evaluating growth opportunities and work-life balance. Each element contributes to a comprehensive framework that transforms decision-making from emotional reaction into strategic planning.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Your Career Decision Framework","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"A thorough job offer assessment requires viewing each opportunity through multiple lenses. Consider how the position serves your immediate needs while advancing your long-term career trajectory. The strongest decisions emerge when compensation, culture, growth potential, and personal values align in meaningful ways.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Reflect on the complete picture rather than isolated factors. A higher salary loses value if the role offers limited advancement or compromises work-life balance. Similarly, an exciting company culture matters less if the compensation structure doesn't support your financial goals.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Taking Action With Confidence","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Armed with your assessment framework, you can approach job offers with clarity and confidence. Review your documented evaluations, weigh priorities against your career goals, and trust the systematic process you've followed. Remember that negotiation remains an option even after initial assessment—use your research to advocate for improvements that better align with your needs.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"When doubt arises, return to your core career objectives. Ask whether this opportunity moves you closer to your professional vision or simply represents a lateral shift. The right decision becomes clearer when viewed through the lens of strategic career development.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"tag":"h3","type":"heading","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Moving Forward","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr"},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Job offer assessment is both an art and a science. While frameworks and checklists provide structure, your unique career goals and personal values ultimately guide the final decision. Trust your preparation, honor your priorities, and choose opportunities that genuinely advance your professional journey.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Every career decision shapes your trajectory. By approaching job offers with thorough assessment and strategic thinking, you position yourself for sustained growth and fulfillment. The time invested in evaluation today prevents regret tomorrow and builds a career aligned with your authentic aspirations.","type":"text","style":"","detail":0,"format":0,"version":1}],"direction":"ltr","textStyle":"","textFormat":0},{"type":"paragraph","format":"","indent":0,"version":1,"children":[{"mode":"normal","text":"Related +export async function acquireRunScopeLock(
+  payload: Payload,

+): Promise&lt;{ acquired: true; ownerToken: string; scopeKey: string } | { acquired: false; scopeKey: string }&gt; {
+  const scopeKey = getRunScopeKey(site)
+  const ownerToken = crypto.randomUUID()
+  const db = (payload as any)?.db?.drizzle
+
+  if (!db?.transaction) {
+    const fallback = await payload.find({
+      collection: 'internal_link_runs',
+      where: {
+        and: [{ lockKey: { equals: scopeKey } }, { status: { equals: 'running' } }],
+      },
+      limit: 1,
+      depth: 0,
+      overrideAccess: true,
+    })
+    if (fallback.docs?.length) return { acquired: false, scopeKey }

+
+  const acquired = await db.transaction(async (tx: any) =&gt; {
+    const conflict =
+      site === 'all'
+        ? await tx.execute(sql&#96;select scope_key from internal_link_run_locks limit 1 for update&#96;)
+        : await tx.execute(sql&#96;
+            select scope_key
+            from internal_link_run_locks
+            where scope_key = 'all' or scope_key = ${scopeKey}
+            limit 1
+            for update
+          &#96;)
+    const rows = Array.isArray(conflict?.rows) ? conflict.rows : []
+    if (rows.length &gt; 0) return false
+
+    await tx.execute(sql&#96;
+      insert into internal_link_run_locks (scope_key, owner_token)
+      values (${scopeKey}, ${ownerToken})
+    &#96;)
+    return true
   })
-  return Boolean(existing.docs?.length)
+
+  if (!acquired) return { acquired: false, scopeKey }
+  return { acquired: true, ownerToken, scopeKey }
+}
+
+export async function releaseRunScopeLock(payload: Payload, scopeKey: string, ownerToken: string): Promise&lt;void&gt; {
+  const db = (payload as any)?.db?.drizzle
+  if (!db?.execute) return
+  await db.execute(sql&#96;
+    delete from internal_link_run_locks
+    where scope_key = ${scopeKey}
+      and owner_token = ${ownerToken}
+  &#96;)
 }

Fixed. The 500 was caused by missing DB columns on `sites`, and I’ve now closed the loop at schema + deploy guardrail level.

## 0) Confirmed root cause (query + schema reality)

Checked `sites` in Postgres and confirmed `revalidate_url` / `revalidate_secret` were missing before fix.  
After applying migration, they now exist:

- `revalidate_secret | text`
- `revalidate_url | text`

## 1) Schema fix implemented (migration path)

Added migration:

- `src/migrations/20260225_add_sites_revalidate_columns.ts`

Registered in:

- `src/migrations/index.ts`

Migration SQL (as requested):

- `ALTER TABLE "sites" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "revalidate_url" text;`
- `ALTER TABLE "sites" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "revalidate_secret" text;`

Executed migrations against prod DB:

- `pnpm payload migrate`  
- Migration ran successfully (`20260225_add_sites_revalidate_columns` applied).

Retest:

- `POST /api/internal-links/run?mode=dry_run&site=all&limit=1` now returns `200` and `runId`.

## 2) Deploy guardrail added so this won’t recur

Updated deploy pipeline to run migrations before stack rollout:

- `scripts/deploy.sh` now executes one-off `pnpm payload migrate` before deploying services.
- Added flag: `--skip-migrations` (default is **run migrations**).
- This is now a guarded, deploy-time schema sync step (not left to replica startup race).

Also re-ran deploy successfully with this flow:
- `./scripts/deploy.sh --force --skip-build`
- Verified runtime env still present:
  - `DATABASE_URI`
  - `PAYLOAD_SECRET`
  - `INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY`

*\\\\\\\\n * Safety: internal Payload calls (relationship population, admin lookups, hooks) all pass\\\\\\\\n * overrideAccess:true. We skip scoping for those so internal data fetching is not broken.\\\\\\\\n *\\\\\\\\n * Validation: if a caller does pass where[site][equals] with a non-integer value (e.g. a\\\\\\\\n * UUID), we return a descriptive 400 instead of letting PostgreSQL crash with a 500.\\\\\\\\n */\\\\\\\\nconst beforeOperation: CollectionBeforeOperationHook = async ({ args, operation }) =\u003e {\\\\\\\\n  if (operation !== 'read') return args\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // Skip internal/system reads — Payload's own calls (relationship population, hooks)\\\\\\\\n  // often use overrideAccess:true. We must not scope those.\\\\\\\\n  if ((args as any).overrideAccess === true) return args\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  const req = (args as any).req\\\\\\\\n  const reqUser = (req as any)?.user\\\\\\\\n  const reqUrl =\\\\\\\\n    typeof (req as any)?.originalUrl === 'string'\\\\\\\\n      ? (req as any).originalUrl\\\\\\\\n      : typeof (req as any)?.url === 'string'\\\\\\\\n        ? (req as any).url\\\\\\\\n        : ''\\\\\\\\n  const referer =\\\\\\\\n    typeof req?.headers?.get === 'function'\\\\\\\\n      ? req.headers.get('referer')\\\\\\\\n      : req?.headers?.referer || req?.headers?.Referer || ''\\\\\\\\n  const isAdminRequest =\\\\\\\\n    /\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\/admin(?:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\/|$)/.test(String(reqUrl)) || /\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\/admin(?:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\/|$)/.test(String(referer))\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // Do not auto-scope authenticated admin reads. Admin users must be able to\\\\\\\\n  // view and manage content across all sites.\\\\\\\\n  if (reqUser \u0026\u0026 isAdminRequest) return args\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  const where = (args as any)?.where\\\\\\\\n  const siteValue = where?.site?.equals\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // If caller explicitly passed a site filter, validate it's a usable integer ID.\\\\\\\\n  // UUID strings cause Number() → NaN → Postgres \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"invalid input syntax for type integer\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" → 500.\\\\\\\\n  if (siteValue != null) {\\\\\\\\n    if (typeof siteValue === 'string' \u0026\u0026 isNaN(Number(siteValue))) {\\\\\\\\n      throw new APIError(\\\\\\\\n        &#96;Invalid site ID \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"${siteValue}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\". The where[site][equals] filter must be a numeric &#96; +\\\\\\\\n          &#96;integer ID — not a UUID or slug. You can omit this filter entirely: the CMS &#96; +\\\\\\\\n          &#96;auto-scopes to the correct site based on the domain you're hitting &#96; +\\\\\\\\n          &#96;(e.g. cms.resumecoach.me → site 1). Use GET /api/sites to list all sites.&#96;,\\\\\\\\n        400,\\\\\\\\n        undefined,\\\\\\\\n        true,\\\\\\\\n      )\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n    // Valid integer provided — let it pass through as-is.\\\\\\\\n    return args\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // No site filter provided — auto-inject from the request domain.\\\\\\\\n  // cms.resumecoach.me → Resume Coach (id: 1), cms.blogcraft.app → BlogCraft (id: 6), etc.\\\\\\\\n  if (req?.payload \u0026\u0026 req?.headers) {\\\\\\\\n    try {\\\\\\\\n      const site = await resolveSiteForRequest(req.payload, req.headers)\\\\\\\\n      if (site?.id) {\\\\\\\\n        ;(args as any).where = {\\\\\\\\n          ...((args as any).where ?? {}),\\\\\\\\n          site: { equals: Number(site.id) },\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n      }\\\\\\\\n    } catch (err) {\\\\\\\\n      // Non-fatal: if site resolution fails, let the query through unscoped\\\\\\\\n      req.payload?.logger?.warn({ err }, 'Articles beforeOperation: site resolution failed, returning unscoped results')\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  return args\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n/**\\\\\\\\n * Resolves a list of category or tag values to integer IDs.\\\\\\\\n *\\\\\\\\n * Make.com sends slugs (or names) instead of IDs because the content pipeline\\\\\\\\n * doesn't have access to Payload's internal integer IDs. a targeted fix for the regression in admin article visibility, with DB-backed investigation to confirm root cause.\\\\n\\\\n### Root cause summary\\\\n\\\\n- The regression is caused by automatic site filter is provided.\\\\n  - On &#96;cms.xencolabs.com&#96;, host resolution maps to &#96;xencolabs&#96; site, so admin reads are scoped to that site.\\\\n- DB evidence from local stack:\\\\n  - &#96;sites&#96; has 21 records (not 2) in &#96;public&#96;.\\\\n  - &#96;xencolabs&#96; site has &#96;0&#96; articles; &#96;sonomagrovesuites&#96; has &#96;91&#96; articles.\\\\n  - So admin at xencolabs domain would legitimately see an empty article list under forced scoping.\\\\n- I also checked schema shape concerns:\\\\n  - &#96;public.sites&#96; schema is valid (&#96;id integer&#96;, expected columns present).\\\\n  - There is another &#96;sites&#96; table in a different schema (&#96;scorecraft&#96;), which can confuse unqualified schema inspection, but Payload is using &#96;public.sites&#96;.\\\\n  - No &#96;public.sites&#96; duplicate &#96;id&#96; column issue found.\\\\n\\\\n### Exact files changed and why\\\\n\\\\n- Updated: &#96;src/collections/Articles.ts&#96;\\\\n  - Added a guard in &#96;beforeOperation&#96; to **skip auto domain-scoping for authenticated admin UI reads** (detected via authenticated request + admin URL/referer).\\\\n  - Kept existing behavior for external/API callers, including numeric-site validation and host-based scoping.\\\\n\\\\nRelevant patch area:\\\\n\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;107:167:src/collections/Articles.ts\\\\nconst beforeOperation: CollectionBeforeOperationHook = async ({ args, operation }) =\u003e {\\\\n  if (operation !== 'read') return args\\\\n\\\\n  // Skip internal/system reads — Payload's own calls (relationship population, hooks)\\\\n  // often use overrideAccess:true. We must not scope those.\\\\n  if ((args as any).overrideAccess === true) return args\\\\n\\\\n  const req = (args as any).req\\\\n  const reqUser = (req as any)?.user\\\\n  const reqUrl =\\\\n    typeof (req as any)?.originalUrl === 'string'\\\\n      ? (req as any).originalUrl\\\\n      : typeof (req as any)?.url === 'string'\\\\n        ? (req as any).url\\\\n        : ''\\\\n  const referer =\\\\n    typeof req?.headers?.get === 'function'\\\\n      ? req.headers.get('referer')\\\\n      : req?.headers?.referer || req?.headers?.Referer || ''\\\\n  const isAdminRequest =\\\\n    /\\\\\\\\/admin(?:\\\\\\\\/|$)/.test(String(reqUrl)) || /\\\\\\\\/admin(?:\\\\\\\\/|$)/.test(String(referer))\\\\n\\\\n  // Do not auto-scope authenticated admin reads. Admin users must be able to\\\\n  // view and manage content across all sites.\\\\n  if (reqUser \u0026\u0026 isAdminRequest) return args\\\\n\\\\n  // ... existing explicit-site validation and auto-scope logic ...\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\n\\\\n### Validation performed and results\\\\n\\\\n- DB validation (via running Postgres container):\\\\n  - &#96;sites&#96; count = &#96;21&#96;\\\\n  - article distribution:\\\\n    - &#96;sonomagrovesuites&#96;: &#96;91&#96;\\\\n    - &#96;xencolabs&#96;: &#96;0&#96;\\\\n  - confirmed active schema: &#96;public.sites&#96; has expected columns only.\\\\n- Code validation:\\\\n  - &#96;pnpm exec eslint src/collections/Articles.ts&#96; → no errors (warnings are pre-existing &#96;any&#96; warnings).\\\\n  - &#96;pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false&#96; → passed.\\\\n  - IDE diagnostics check on edited file → no new lint errors.\\\\n\\\\n### Follow-up risks / notes\\\\n\\\\n- The admin bypass depends on admin-request detection (&#96;/admin&#96; in URL/referer). If a proxy strips referer and URL shape is unusual, admin requests could still be scoped.\\\\n- If that occurs, next hardening step is to bypass scoping for all authenticated Payload users (broader from '../lib/revalidate'\\n\\n\\n\\nlet cachedDefaultSiteId: string | null = null\\nlet cachedDefaultSiteAt = 0\\n\\nasync function getDefaultSiteId(req: {\\n  payload: { find: (args: any) =\u003e Promise\u003cany\u003e }\\n}): Promise\u003cstring | null\u003e {\\n  const now = Date.now()\\n  if (cachedDefaultSiteId \u0026\u0026 now - cachedDefaultSiteAt \u003c 60_000) return cachedDefaultSiteId\\n\\n  const res = await req.payload.find({\\n    collection: 'sites',\\n    where: { isDefault: { equals: true } },\\n    limit: 1,\\n    depth: 0,\\n    overrideAccess: true,\\n  })\\n\\n  const site = res.docs?.[0]\\n  if (!site?.id) return null\\n\\n  cachedDefaultSiteId = String(site.id)\\n  cachedDefaultSiteAt = now\\n  return cachedDefaultSiteId\\n}\\n\\nfunction slugify(input: string): string {\\n  return input\\n    .trim()\\n    .toLowerCase()\\n    .replace(/['\\\"]/g, '')\\n    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')\\n    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')\\n}\\n\\nasync function ensureUniqueSlugForSite(args: {\\n  req: any\\n  siteId: string\\n  slug: string\\n  currentId?: string\\n}): Promise\u003cstring\u003e {\\n  const base = slugify(args.slug)\\n  let candidate = base\\n  let i = 2\\n\\n  while (true) {\\n    // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any\\n    const where: any = {\\n      and: [{ site: { equals: args.siteId } }, { slug: { equals: candidate } }],\\n    }\\n\\n    // exclude current doc on updates\\n    if (args.currentId) {\\n      where.and.push({ id: { not_equals: args.currentId } })\\n    }\\n\\n    const existing = await args.req.payload.find({\\n      collection: 'articles',\\n      where,\\n      limit: 1,\\n      depth: 0,\\n      overrideAccess: true,\\n    })\\n\\n    if (!existing.docs?.length) return candidate\\n    candidate = &#96;${base}-${i++}&#96;\\n    if (i \u003e 50) throw new Error('Unable to generate unique slug for this site.')\\n  }\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * Domain-based site scoping for read operations.\\n *\\n * The CMS is multi-tenant: cms.resumecoach.me, cms.blogcraft.app, etc. each map to a\\n * specific Site record. This logic was already applied on writes (beforeChange). This hook\\n * extends it to reads so that external callers (Make.com, frontends, APIs) hitting a\\n * domain-specific CMS URL automatically see only that site's articles — no need to\\n * manually pass where[site][equals] at all.\\n *\\n * Safety: internal Payload calls (relationship population, admin lookups, hooks) all pass\\n * overrideAccess:true. We skip scoping for those so internal data fetching is not broken.\\n *\\n * Validation: if a caller does pass where[site][equals] with a non-integer value (e.g. a\\n * UUID), we return a descriptive 400 instead of letting PostgreSQL crash with a 500.\\n */\\nconst beforeOperation: CollectionBeforeOperationHook = async ({ args, operation }) =\u003e {\\n  if (operation !== 'read') return args\\n\\n  // Skip internal/system reads — Payload's own calls (relationship population, hooks,\\n  // admin operations) use overrideAccess:true. We must not scope those.\\n  if ((args as any).overrideAccess === true) return args\\n\\n  const where = (args as any)?.where\\n  const siteValue = where?.site?.equals\\n\\n  // If caller explicitly passed a site filter, validate it's a usable integer ID.\\n  // UUID strings cause Number() → NaN → Postgres \\\"invalid input syntax for type integer\\\" → 500.\\n  if (siteValue != null) {\\n    if (typeof siteValue === 'string' \u0026\u0026 isNaN(Number(siteValue))) {\\n      throw new APIError(\\n        &#96;Invalid site ID \\\"${siteValue}\\\". The where[site][equals] filter must be a numeric &#96; +\\n          &#96;integer ID — not a UUID or slug. You can omit this filter entirely: the CMS &#96; +\\n          &#96;auto-scopes to the correct site based on the domain you're hitting &#96; +\\n          &#96;(e.g. cms.resumecoach.me → site 1). Use GET /api/sites to list all sites.&#96;,\\n        400,\\n        undefined,\\n        true,\\n      )\\n    }\\n    // Valid integer provided — let it pass through as-is.\\n    return args\\n  }\\n\\n  // No site filter provided — auto-inject from the request domain.\\n  // cms.resumecoach.me → Resume Coach (id: 1), cms.blogcraft.app → BlogCraft (id: 6), etc.\\n  const req = (args as any).req\\n  if (req?.payload \u0026\u0026 req?.headers) {\\n    try {\\n      const site = await resolveSiteForRequest(req.payload, req.headers)\\n      if (site?.id) {\\n        ;(args as any).where = {\\n          ...((args as any).where ?? {}),\\n          site: { equals: Number(site.id) },\\n        }\\n      }\\n    } catch (err) {\\n      // Non-fatal: if site resolution fails, let the query through unscoped\\n      req.payload?.logger?.warn({ err }, 'Articles beforeOperation: site resolution failed, returning unscoped results')\\n    }\\n  }\\n\\n  return args\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * Resolves a list of category or tag values to integer IDs.\\n *\\n * Make.com sends slugs (or names) instead of IDs because the content pipeline\\n * doesn't have access to Payload's internal integer IDs. This resolver accepts\\n * a mixed array of integers and/or strings, looks up each string by slug first\\n * then by title/name, and returns a clean array of integer IDs.\\n *\\n * Items that are already integers pass through unchanged (backward compatible).\\n * Strings that don't match any record are logged and dropped.\\n */\\nasync function resolveRelationIds(\\n  payload: { find: (args: any) =\u003e Promise\u003cany\u003e; logger: any },\\n  collection: 'categories' | 'tags',\\n  values: any[],\\n  siteId: string | null,\\n): Promise\u003cnumber[]\u003e {\\n  const ids: number[] = []\\n\\n  for (const val of values) {\\n    // Already a valid integer ID — pass through\\n    if (typeof val === 'number' \u0026\u0026 Number.isInteger(val)) {\\n      ids.push(val)\\n      continue\\n    }\\n    if (typeof val === 'string' \u0026\u0026 /^\\\\d+$/.test(val)) {\\n      ids.push(Number(val))\\n      continue\\n    }\\n\\n    // String slug or name — look it up\\n    if (typeof val === 'string') {\\n      const nameField = collection === 'categories' ? 'title' : 'name'\\n      const siteFilter = siteId ? [{ site: { equals: Number(siteId) } }] : []\\n\\n      // Try slug first, then title/name\\n      for (const filter of [{ slug: { equals: val } }, { [nameField]: { equals: val } }]) {\\n        const res = await payload.find({\\n          collection,\\n          where: siteFilter.length ? { and: [filter, ...siteFilter] } : filter,\\n          limit: 1,\\n          depth: 0,\\n          overrideAccess: true,\\n        })\\n        const found = res.docs?.[0]\\n        if (found?.id) {\\n          ids.push(Number(found.id))\\n          break\\n        }\\n      }\\n\\n      if (!ids.length || ids[ids.length - 1] === undefined) {\\n        payload.logger.warn(\\n          &#96;Articles beforeChange: ${collection} slug/name \\\"${val}\\\" not found for site ${siteId ?? 'any'} — skipping&#96;,\\n        )\\n      }\\n      continue\\n    }\\n\\n    // Object with id property (e.g. already-populated relationship)\\n    if (val \u0026\u0026 typeof val === 'object' \u0026\u0026 val.id) {\\n      ids.push(Number(val.id))\\n    }\\n  }\\n\\n  return ids\\n}\\n\\n/**\\n * Recursively walks a Lexical node tree and normalises upload nodes that were\\n * built with the wrong structure by Make.com's content pipeline.\\n *\\n * Make.com sends:  { \\\"type\\\":\\\"upload\\\", \\\"version\\\":2, \\\"id\\\":243, \\\"fields\\\":null, ... }\\n * Payload expects: { \\\"type\\\":\\\"upload\\\", \\\"version\\\":1, \\\"value\\\":243, \\\"fields\\\":{}, ... }\\n *\\n * Differences:\\n *   - version 2 → 1\\n *   - id: N (top-level integer) → value: N\\n *   - fields: null → fields: {}\\n */\\nfunction sanitizeLexicalUploads(node: any): any {\\n  if (!node || typeof node !== 'object') return node\\n\\n  if (Array.isArray(node)) {\\n    return node.map(sanitizeLexicalUploads)\\n  }\\n\\n  if (node.type === 'upload') {\\n    const fixed: any = { ...node }\\n\\n    // version: always 1 for Payload Lexical upload nodes\\n    fixed.version = 1\\n\\n    // value: the media integer ID. Make.com puts it in \\\"id\\\"; Payload expects \\\"value\\\".\\n    if (fixed.value == null \u0026\u0026 fixed.id != null \u0026\u0026 typeof fixed.id === 'number') {\\n      fixed.value = fixed.id\\n      delete fixed.id\\n    }\\n\\n    // fields must be an object — null causes \\\"not a valid upload ID\\\" validation failure\\n    if (fixed.fields == null) {\\n      fixed.fields = {}\\n    }\\n\\n    // Ensure required Lexical node props are present\\n    if (fixed.format == null) fixed.format = ''\\n    if (fixed.indent == null) fixed.indent = 0\\n\\n    // Recurse into _**Agent (gpt-5.3-codex)**_

Root cause found and fixed.

- **Primary issue:** admin article reads were being auto-scoped by request domain in `Articles` read hook, the same way public/API reads are scoped.
- **Why you saw “no articles”:** on `cms.xencolabs.com`, domain resolution mapped to the `xencolabs` site, which currently has `0` articles, while Sonoma has content.
- **Secondary confusion checked:** `sites` data/schema was validated in the active `public` schema; no active duplicate-ID problem there causing this specific symptom.

### What I changed

Updated `src/collections/Articles.ts` to bypass domain auto-scoping for authenticated admin UI requests, while keeping domain scoping for external/API callers.

```107:132:src/collections/Articles.ts
const beforeOperation: CollectionBeforeOperationHook = async ({ args, operation }) => {
  if (operation !== 'read') return args

  if ((args as any).overrideAccess === true) return args

  const req = (args as any).req
  const reqUser = (req as any)?.user
  const reqUrl =
    typeof (req as any)?.originalUrl === 'string'
      ? (req as any).originalUrl
      : typeof (req as any)?.url === 'string'
        ? (req as any).url
        : ''
  const referer =
    typeof req?.headers?.get === 'function'
      ? req.headers.get('referer')
      : req?.headers?.referer || req?.headers?.Referer || ''
  const isAdminRequest =
    /\/admin(?:\/|$)/.test(String(reqUrl)) || /\/admin(?:\/|$)/.test(String(referer))

  if (reqUser && isAdminRequest) return args
```

### Validation performed

- Lint/type checks on touched logic passed (warnings only, no blocking errors).
- Built and redeployed stack with guarded deploy flow.
- Service health after deploy:
  - `payload-postgres_postgres` = `1/1`
  - `payload-swarm_payload` = `3/3`
- Health endpoints are up and returning `200` from deploy verification.

### What to test now in UI

1. Log into `cms.xencolabs.com` as main admin.
2. Open Articles list: should no longer appear empty just because of host scoping.
3. Switch/filter to Sonoma Grove Suites and confirm expected articles appear.

If you want, I can now add a stricter safeguard so **all authenticated admin users** always bypass domain auto-scope (not just `/admin` URL detection), which would make this even harder to regress.

_**User**_

I've added the www cname, and I've added cms.SonomaGroveSuites three times and saved it, and it said it was saved. Then I switched screens, refreshed, came back, and it says it saves the domains are not persistent. The user I created, it's the second time I've created this user. It only persists with Xencolabs and then the other admin one, so something's going on with the database. It's saying it's saving the changes, but they're not persisting. I need you to check and find out what's happening because something's not right.

_**Agent (gpt-5.3-codex)**_

You were right to flag this — I found what was happening.

### What I found

- **DB persistence is working.**  
  I checked Postgres directly:
  - Sonoma user exists in `public.users` (`xen@sonomagrovesuites.com`).
  - Sonoma site exists in `public.sites`.
- The “domains not persistent” behavior was caused by **save-time normalization logic** in `Sites`:
  - It was intentionally stripping `cms.` and `www.` and deduping to root domain.
  - So entering:
    - `sonomagrovesuites.com`
    - `www.sonomagrovesuites.com`
    - `cms.sonomagrovesuites.com`
  - got collapsed to just:
    - `sonomagrovesuites.com`
  - After refresh, it looked like values were “lost” even though the save succeeded.

### Fix applied

I changed `src/collections/Sites.ts` so domains are still normalized (lowercase, no protocol/port/path), but **subdomains are preserved** (`cms.` / `www.` are no longer stripped on save).

So now those 3 entries will remain 3 entries after save/refresh.

### Deployed

I built/pushed/redeployed with the new guardrailed deploy flow, and service health is good (`payload-swarm` 3/3, health endpoints OK).

### What to do now

Please re-test in admin:

1. Open Sonoma Grove Suites site.
2. Add:
   - `sonomagrovesuites.com`
   - `www.sonomagrovesuites.com`
   - `cms.sonomagrovesuites.com`
3. Save, refresh, reopen.

Those should now persist exactly as entered.

If you want, next I can also add a small admin help note under `domains` saying “we preserve exact subdomains; no auto-collapse,” so behavior is explicit for future admins.

---

_**User**_

Okay, I was able to log in. I created a new user. Listen, my Opus Architect has some because we're having issues on the Sonoma Grove Suites site, especially with the site map. Here are some instructions that we need you to verify and/or fix and then give us the summary.

The Payload admin's fix only bypasses domain scoping for authenticated admin UI requests. When the Next.js sitemap generator calls cms.xencolabs.com/api/articles server-side, it's using the API key, not an admin session. So the domain-scoping hook still kicks in, resolves cms.xencolabs.com to the xencolabs site (not Sonoma), and the query returns zero results even though the where clause specifies site=10.
The blog pages themselves work because they're force-dynamic and presumably the getBlogPostDetailBySlug query succeeds — but it might be succeeding for a different reason (maybe the slug-based lookup bypasses the scope, or the API key auth path works differently).
What needs to happen:
Tell the Payload admin: the domain-scoping bypass needs to also apply to API key authenticated requests, not just admin UI requests. The Next.js frontend authenticates via PAYLOAD_USER_API_KEY and passes site=10 explicitly in every query. The beforeOperation hook should not add additional domain-based scoping when the caller is already filtering by site ID. The fix should be:
typescript// Also bypass domain scoping for API key authenticated requests
const isApiKeyAuth = reqUser && reqUser.apiKey; // or however API key users are identified
if ((reqUser && isAdminRequest) || isApiKeyAuth) return args;
Or more robustly: if the query's where clause already contains a site filter, don't add domain scoping on top of it. That's the correct architectural fix — the caller is being explicit about which site they want.
Once that's fixed, redeploy the Payload CMS, then hit /sitemap.xml again. You should see all the blog posts, category pages, directory entries, and events appear.

---

Confirmed and fixed the Payload-side issue your architect described.

## What I verified

- Your diagnosis was correct: the old hook only recognized explicit site filters in one narrow shape (`where.site.equals`), so nested filters could still get extra domain scoping injected.
- I updated the `Articles` read hook to:
  - bypass domain scoping for API-key-auth signals, and
  - **most importantly** detect site constraints anywhere in `where` (nested `and/or`) and never inject domain scope if caller is explicit.

## Fix applied

Updated `src/collections/Articles.ts`:

- Added recursive site-filter detection:
  - `collectSiteEqualsValues(...)`
  - `hasAnySiteConstraint(...)`
- Added API-key auth signal check:
  - `hasApiKeyAuthSignal(req)`
- Behavior now:
  - if admin request or API-key request → no domain auto-scope injection
  - if query already has any `site` constraint (any shape) → no domain auto-scope injection
  - still validates `site.equals` values for bad non-numeric IDs

## Validation results

- Redeployed Payload successfully with guarded deploy flow.
- Live API-key test (against `cms.xencolabs.com`) now returns Sonoma data correctly:

`GET /api/articles?where[site][equals]=10&where[status][equals]=published&limit=2&depth=0`  
with `Authorization: users API-Key <key>` returned `totalDocs: 91` and Sonoma articles (site `10`), including:
- `al-fresco-dining-9-best-ultimate-wine-experiences-in-sonoma`
- `review-cha-11`

That confirms domain scoping is no longer overriding explicit site filtering for this path.

## Important follow-up: sitemap still missing blog entries

I checked `https://sonomagrovesuites.com/sitemap.xml` after deploy.  
It currently contains only 11 static top-level URLs (`/`, `/blog`, `/events`, etc.) and **does not include article URLs**.

So:
- Payload fix is working.
