/dev-debugger   What to test next (do these in order)
Test 1 — Concurrency retest (confirm whether locking is still broken)

Run 5 parallel requests to the same scope. Expected: 1×200, 4×409.

# Replace KEY with INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY value
export KEY="REDACTED"
export BASE="https://cms.resumecoach.me"   # or whatever your Payload base is

seq 1 5 | xargs -n1 -P5 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
  -X POST "$BASE/api/internal-links/run?mode=dry_run&site=all&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"

What you collect: the HTTP codes output + the runId from the one 200 response + GET /api/internal-links/runs/{runId}.

If you still see multiple 200s, locking is still not atomic and must be fixed before cron.

Test 2 — Generate a deterministic edge dataset (so we can prove active/stale + revert)

Right now your dry run shows skippedNoMatch=11 and fallbackInserted=0, and apply produced no updates. That’s why internal_link_edges=0.

Do this controlled setup:

Step A: Create one internal link rule that is guaranteed to match

In Payload Admin:

Create a target article: pick a stable evergreen post (Target)

Pick a source article that contains an exact phrase you can match (Source)

Create one InternalLinkRule:

site = 1

targetArticle = <Target>

keywords = ["Applicant Tracking System"] (or any phrase that definitely appears in Source)

priority = 100

maxLinksPerSource = 1

enabled = true

Step B: Apply with tiny limit
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/api/internal-links/run?mode=apply&site=1&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | jq

Expected: updated >= 1 and linksInserted >= 1.
Then confirm edges exist:

select count(*) from internal_link_edges;

(or via Payload admin collection view)

What you collect: apply response + GET /api/internal-links/runs/{applyRunId} + one InternalLinkEdges row screenshot/json for that source article.

Test 3 — Create an active + stale edge artifact (prove reconciliation)

Now that at least one edge exists:

Manually remove the inserted link in the Source article (Payload Admin edit content).

Run apply again (same site, small limit):

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/api/internal-links/run?mode=apply&site=1&limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | jq

Expected behavior (after reconciliation exists):

The previously inserted edge becomes status=stale (or is_active=false)

Any currently present inserted links remain active

What you collect:

Screenshot/json of edges for the source article showing at least:

one active

one stale

And a snippet of the article content showing the link is actually gone/present.

If you don’t see any active/stale change, reconciliation either isn’t implemented yet or isn’t being invoked in apply.

Test 4 — Revert run summary (prove rollback works on real inserts)

Now revert the run that inserted the link (the apply runId from Test 2):

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/api/internal-links/revert?runId=<APPLY_RUN_ID>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | jq

Then:

curl -s "$BASE/api/internal-links/runs/<REVERT_RUN_ID>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | jq

What you collect: revert response + revert run record + one edge row showing status=reverted (and the link removed from content).

Why your lock.ts is still suspicious (even after the 500 fix)

This pattern can still race:

SELECT … FOR UPDATE locks rows only if they exist

If the lock table is empty, both transactions can see “no rows” and both insert

To make it atomic you need at least one of:

internal_link_run_locks.scope_key UNIQUE/PK and insert uses conflict handling, or

an explicit LOCK TABLE internal_link_run_locks before checking, or

Postgres advisory locks (pg_try_advisory_lock) (best), or

Redis SET NX with value-checked release (if you can’t rely on DB locks)

So after the concurrency retest, if it still fails, the admin should implement one of those.


The easiest “evidence packet” is for them to paste:
One run record (GET /api/internal-links/runs/{id})
One edge list filtered by a source article showing active/stale
One revert run record showing revertedCount>0

edge lifecycle reconciliation (&#96;active|stale|reverted&#96;)\\\\\\\\n- run-level rollback endpoint\\\\\\\\n- site slug support\\\\\\\\n- API key management via env + Docker Swarm secrets\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 1) Environment and Secrets Source of Truth\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nPrimary source of truth:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;.env.production&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRequired keys for linker operations:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;PAYLOAD_SECRET&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;DATABASE_URI&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;REDIS_PASSWORD&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSwarm secrets expected:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;payload_secret&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;internal_linker_api_key&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;postgres_password&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe stack mounts:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;/run/secrets/internal_linker_api_key&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nAnd also sets:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY&#96; (env)\\\\\\\\n- &#96;INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/internal_linker_api_key&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nAPI auth checks use env first and fallback to file.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 2) Deploy-Time &#96;docker stack deploy&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 3) Internal Linker Endpoints\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nRun:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\\\\\\\\ncurl -sS -X POST \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"https://publish.xencolabs.com/api/internal-links/run?mode=dry_run\u0026site=all\u0026limit=20\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  -H \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"x-api-key: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"https://publish.xencolabs.com/api/internal-links/revert?runId=\u003cRUN_ID\u003e\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  -H \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"x-api-key: $INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nSite token rules:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;site=all&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;site=\u003cnumeric id\u003e&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;site=\u003cslug token\u003e&#96; (example: &#96;site=resumecoach&#96;)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 4) Concurrency and Scope Semantics\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nLock behavior:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;site=all&#96; blocks all concurrent runs\\\\\\\\n- &#96;site=\u003cid\u003e&#96; blocks same site runs\\\\\\\\n- &#96;site=\u003cid\u003e&#96; is blocked while &#96;site=all&#96; is running\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nExpected responses under contention:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- winner: &#96;200&#96;\\\\\\\\n- blocked contenders: &#96;409&#96; with &#96;Run already in progress&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 5) Edge Lifecycle Semantics\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nEach edge can be:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;active&#96;: link is currently present in source content\\\\\\\\n- &#96;stale&#96;: edge exists historically but link is no longer present\\\\\\\\n- &#96;reverted&#96;: removed by explicit revert run\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nFields used:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;status&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;lastSeenRunId&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;revertRunId&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;targetUrl&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;fingerprint&#96;\\\\\\\\n- &#96;leftContext&#96; / &#96;rightContext&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 6) Verification Checklist (Post-Deploy)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n1. Auth check:\\\\\\\\n   - run a small dry run with API key, expect &#96;200&#96;\\\\\\\\n2. Lock check:\\\\\\\\n   - fire 5 parallel &#96;site=all&#96; dry runs, expect &#96;1x200 + 4x409&#96;\\\\\\\\n3. Scope check:\\\\\\\\n   - run &#96;site=1&#96; and &#96;site=10&#96; in parallel, expect both &#96;200&#96;\\\\\\\\n4. Slug check:\\\\\\\\n   - run &#96;site=resumecoach&#96;, expect &#96;200&#96; and resolved to site &#96;1&#96;\\\\\\\\n5. Revert check:\\\\\\\\n   - apply with small limit, then revert by run ID, confirm &#96;reverted&#96; edge statuses\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## 7) Notes\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- If secret values are rotated, update &#96;.env.production&#96; and explicitly rotate/recreate Swarm secrets as part of maintenance.\\\\\\\\n- Keep &#96;INTERNAL_LINKER_API_KEY&#96; out of logs and tickets; use env/substitution during ## Result Summary

- **Test 3 (Active/Stale reconciliation):** succeeded — got one `stale` and one `active` edge on the same source article after manual link removal + apply.
- **Test 4 (Revert):** succeeded — revert run executed, `revertedCount > 0`, and link removed from content.

## Evidence Packet (key artifacts)

### 1) Concurrency retest

Observed codes (parallel 5 requests):
- Run A: `409,409,409,409,409`
- Run B: `409,409,409,000(timeout),409`

During Run B, server created winner run:
- `runId: 15`, status `running`, lockKey `internal-linker:all`

So one request did win, others conflicted; the `000` was transport timeout while server accepted that run.

### 2) Deterministic edge dataset

- Created deterministic rules for site `1`.
- Dry run response (prereq): `runId: 8`, `status: succeeded`

- `id: 5`
- `status: active`
- `runId: 9`
- `sourceArticleId: 7`
- `targetUrl: /ats-keywords-vs-keyword-stuffing-2026`

### 3) Active + stale proof

After manually removing one inserted link from source article `22` and re-running apply (`runId: 13`), edge states for same source article became:

- Edge 1: `status: stale` (target `...keyword-stuffing-2026`)
- Edge 2: `status: active` (target `...keywords-2026-without-sounding-fake`)

Content checks also matched:
- removed target link count: `0`
- kept target link count: `1`

### 4) Revert proof

Reverted apply run `9`:

- Revert response:
  - `{"ok":true,"runId":"14","status":"reverted","revertedCount":4,"failedCount":0}`
- Revert run record `14`:

  - `action: revert`
  - `revertedCount: 4`
- Edge proof:
  - edge `id: 5` now `status: reverted`, `revertRunId: 14`
- Content proof:
  - target link removed from article `7` (`link_nodes=0`)

Some apply runs return: **“The following field is invalid: Author”** and mark run `failed`, even while linker writes still happen.  
That’s a separate data-validation issue worth fixing next, but it did not block producing the active/stale/revert lifecycle evidence.

_**Agent (gpt-5.3-codex)**_

I’ve isolated why 500s still happen under race: the DB duplicate-key exception shape in production isn’t always a standard `Error`, so my first catch didn’t match. I’m patching lock error handling to detect Postgres unique-violation by `code=23505` and nested `message/cause`, then redeploying and re-running the concurrency proof.

Implemented the hardening changes in this repo and validated the linker behavior in production.

## What I changed

- Fixed the `Author invalid` root cause in `Articles` update hooks:
  - `src/collections/Articles.ts`
  - On `update`, when `site` is not explicitly provided, it now **does not infer site from host** (which was re-scoping some updates and breaking author relation validation).
- Kept linker article updates content-only:
  - `src/lib/internal-linker/runner.ts`
  - Article patch path remains `data: { content }` only (plus optional future `internalLinkedAt` support).
- Added a test that enforces article update payload keys:
  - `tests/int/internal-linker-runner-payload.int.spec.ts`
  - Asserts article update payload contains only `content` (and optionally `internalLinkedAt`).
- Hardened lock race conflict handling:
  - `src/lib/internal-linker/lock.ts`
  - Added robust duplicate-key detection (including Postgres `23505`/nested error shapes) so races return conflict behavior instead of 500s.
- Improved run responsiveness without brittle in-request background workers:
  - `src/lib/internal-linker/runner.ts`
  - `limit` now acts as a processing cap per site in-run, so `site=all&limit=1` stays bounded and avoids long-running endpoint hangs.
  - `src/endpoints/internalLinksRun.ts`
  - Kept endpoint deterministic/synchronous with proper locking and better auth header parsing (`x-api-key`, `Bearer`, `Users API-Key`).

## Deliverables

- **Clean apply run JSON (no author error):**
  - `POST /api/internal-links/run?mode=apply&site=1&limit=1`
  - Response:
    - `{"ok":true,"runId":"22","status":"succeeded", ...}`
  - Run record `id=22`:
    - `status: "succeeded"`
    - `errors: []`
- **Concurrency proof (single winner + conflicts, no 000):**
  - Parallel 5x on `mode=dry_run&site=all&limit=1`
  - Final stable result: `409 409 200 409 409`
  - Winner run: `id=20` (`status: "succeeded"`)

## Exact prior “Author invalid” payload + code path

- Prior failing run payload had:
  - `errors: [{ "message": "The following field is invalid: Author" }]`
- Likely failing path was:
  - `runInternalLinker()` in `src/lib/internal-linker/runner.ts` calling `payload.update({ collection: 'articles', data: { content } })`
  - Triggering `beforeChange` in `src/collections/Articles.ts`, which previously could infer/overwrite `site` from request host on update; that could invalidate existing `author` relation constraints.

## Sonoma sitemap integration status

- I verified Payload now returns Sonoma content correctly when explicitly filtered:
  - `GET /api/articles?where[site][equals]=10&where[status][equals]=published&limit=100`
  - returns `totalDocs: 230`.
- Current live sitemap still shows no blog detail URLs:
  - `https://sonomagrovesuites.com/sitemap.xml` currently has `blog_locs: 0`.
- I could not safely patch the Sonoma frontend sitemap code from this repo because that sitemap source file is not present here.

If you share the exact Sonoma frontend repo/path (or open that workspace), I’ll patch its `sitemap.ts` immediately to emit `/blog/{slug}` URLs from Payload for the Sonoma site and verify 50+ URLs plus live route resolution.

* ✅ Locking now behaves as expected (1 winner + 409s, no timeouts)

* ✅ Auth parsing hardened

So the Payload-side internal-linker is **green**.
